title: Developing Creativity
overview: Creativity is a practical capability that enables individuals and teams to look beyond habitual solutions, challenge assumptions, connect ideas in new ways, and develop useful alternatives to familiar problems. In professional environments, creativity supports problem solving, service improvement, innovation, communication, planning, and the ability to respond constructively to changing requirements.

This course develops creativity as a structured and trainable skill. Participants will explore how creative thinking works, identify personal and organizational barriers, strengthen curiosity and observation, practice divergent and convergent thinking, reframe problems, generate ideas using a range of techniques, combine and develop concepts, and evaluate ideas without eliminating promising possibilities too early.

The program is highly practical and emphasizes application. Participants will work through individual and group creativity challenges, use structured tools such as brainstorming, brainwriting, SCAMPER, mind mapping, forced connections, analogies, reversal, and assumption challenging, and develop a personal approach for applying creative thinking to real workplace situations.
audience: Managers, supervisors, team leaders, professionals, project personnel, administrators, service-development staff, innovation teams, problem solvers, and employees at all levels who need to generate ideas, improve existing approaches, solve problems creatively, or contribute more effectively to organizational innovation.
methodology: The course uses an experiential methodology combining short presentations, creativity diagnostics, individual and group challenges, observation exercises, problem-reframing activities, brainstorming and brainwriting, SCAMPER, mind mapping, analogy exercises, forced connections, assumption challenges, idea-development workshops, evaluation activities, and workplace application exercises. Participants will repeatedly move from problem definition through idea generation, development, selection, and practical application.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Explain creativity as a practical and developable professional capability.
Identify personal, cognitive, and organizational barriers that restrict creative thinking.
Use observation, curiosity, and questioning to discover new possibilities.
Reframe problems and challenges to open different solution paths.
Apply divergent-thinking techniques to generate a wider range of ideas.
Use structured creativity tools such as brainstorming, brainwriting, SCAMPER, mind mapping, analogies, and forced connections.
Challenge assumptions and habitual ways of thinking.
Combine, extend, and improve initial ideas into stronger concepts.
Apply appropriate criteria to evaluate ideas without suppressing creativity prematurely.
Contribute effectively to group creativity sessions.
Develop a practical personal plan for using creativity in everyday work.
